chunks: Whenever one of you has a pregnancy with a woman and four months have passed over her, let him face her toward the Qiblah and let him recite Ayat al-Kursi (2:255), and let him strike upon her side and let him say: 'O Allah, I have named him Muhammad.' Thus it will make him a boy.

Then if he is faithful to the name, Allah will bless him in it; and if he retracts from the name, the choice will belong to Allah therein — if He wills, He takes him (back), and if He wills, He leaves him.

key_terms.آيَةَ الْكُرْسِيِّ: Ayat al-Kursi — Quran 2:255, the Verse of the Throne, considered the greatest verse of the Quran and widely used for protection and blessing
key_terms.الْخِيَارُ: Al-khiyar — the right of choice; here attributed to Allah regarding the fate of the child if the naming intention is not fulfilled

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq prescribe to do during pregnancy at four months for the birth of a male child?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribed a ritual for a pregnant woman at four months: the husband should face her toward the Qiblah, recite Ayat al-Kursi, pat her side, and declare the intention to name the child Muhammad — this practice is said to result in the birth of a son. The hadith further states that fulfilling this naming intention brings divine blessing, while abandoning it returns the outcome to God's discretion. This teaching reflects the Shia tradition's integration of pious intentions, Quran recitation, and the baraka of prophetic names in pre-natal religious practice.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bni Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Najran, from Al Husayn Bin Ahmad Al Minqary, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Whenever one of you were to have a pregnancy with a woman, so four months come upon her, so let her face the Qiblah and let her recite the Verse of the Throne [2:255], and let her strike upon her side and let her say, ‘O Allahazwj! I have named him Muhammad’.

Thus, if he were to be loyal with the naming, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Bless for him with regards to it, and if he retracts from the naming, there would be for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> a Choice in it, if He<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires to He<sup>azwj</sup> Takes him (back), and if He<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires to, Leaves him’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu Najran from al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Minqariy from certain persons of our people who have said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If the wife of one you is pregnant, during the fourth month ask her to face al-Qiblah (al-Ka‘bah) and read verse 255 of Chapter two, then tap on her side and say, ‘O Lord, I have named him Muhammad.’ Allah will make him a boy.
If he keeps the name as he had promised Allah grants him blessings but if he changes his mind about the name Allah will have the choice to decide to keep the child alive or take him back.”’
